own_solution.law: Calorimetry energy balance: m_w c (dTw - theta) = m_i L + m_i c theta; heat given up Q = m_w c (dTw - theta)
assumptions: all ice melts (stated, and consistent: theta > 0)
ice initially at 0 C, constant c

defect_reasons.other: For T96AB/T5D2A the reader must decide whether 'starts 40 K above the melting point' is the temperature before or after the 17 K heating; I read it as before (water enters mixing 57 K above), and T5D2A's 'the container' is slightly ambiguous now that a second container is present.

notes: Base: 2093(40 - theta) = 26720 + 334.88 theta -> theta = 57000/2427.88 = 23.4773 K; Q = 2093 x 16.5227 = 34582.1 J. With 17 K pre-heating: 2093(57 - theta) = 26720 + 334.88 theta -> theta = 92581/2427.88 = 38.1325 K; Q = 39489.8 J. Heat supplied by the heater is not counted as heat given up during mixing. Second-container and earlier-run sentences are D; T2F5B and T162D carry no number.
